identity.kind: Mercedes automatic transmission gearbox (torque converter included/attached)

claims.claim: Transmissions Gearbox M278 1282 OEM G63, Mercedes transmission gearbox.
claims.evidence: The seller’s text mentions M278 1282 and G63, but the photos do not show a clearly readable model/part number that confirms this.
No shipping/import documents, VIN/part-number paperwork, or Belgium sourcing evidence is visible in the photos.

claims.claim: Tested and working, no knock, low mileage, never opened.
claims.evidence: Photos show a used gearbox with grime; there is no video/test sheet, no diagnostic readout, and no seal/fastener evidence that proves it was never opened.

risks.risk: Wrong transmission variant/part number for the specific Mercedes application (gearbox codes differ even within similar models).
risks.proof: A clear close-up photo of the transmission identification plate/label (part number + gearbox code) and/or the stamped code on the casing, plus the VIN of the donor vehicle (or at least the exact model/engine).
risks.if_unproven: Price as the wrong/unknown variant risk: treat as not guaranteed compatible until the exact gearbox code is confirmed.

risks.risk: Condition not truly proven (internal wear, delayed engagement, slipping, or noise may not be visible in photos).
risks.proof: A short video of the transmission being tested (engage P/R, show no abnormal noise) or a diagnostic scan report showing live data/solenoid operation and no stored faults.
risks.if_unproven: Price as not proven working: treat as needs inspection/possible overhaul risk.

risks.risk: “Never opened” may be false; seals/gaskets may have been replaced or the unit may have been previously repaired.
risks.proof: Photos of all external fasteners/seams, especially around the pan/valve body access points, and close-ups of gasket/seal surfaces (look for fresh sealant, tool marks).
risks.if_unproven: Price as possibly opened/repaired: assume unknown internal history.

risks.risk: Fluid contamination or leaks (dark staining/grime could indicate leaks or old fluid).
risks.proof: Photo of the transmission after cleaning plus close-ups of suspected leak points; also ask for the fluid condition (color/smell) and whether it was drained for testing.
risks.if_unproven: Price as potential leak/contamination risk: assume may require reseal/flush.

risks.risk: Torque converter/related components may be damaged even if the casing looks intact.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of the torque converter mounting surface and any visible scoring; plus a test showing stall/lock-up behavior (or converter part number).
risks.if_unproven: Price as converter condition unknown: assume possible converter replacement risk.

proof_requests: Clear close-up of the transmission identification label/plate (part number + gearbox code) on photo 0 area.
A video showing the gearbox being tested (engage P/R and demonstrate no knock/abnormal noise).
Diagnostic scan report (fault codes + live data) from the test setup, if available.
Photos of all gasket/seal lines and any access-pan/valve-body areas to support “never opened.”
Donor vehicle details (VIN or at least exact model/engine) to confirm compatibility with the claimed G63/M278.
response.reason: The photos confirm it is a Mercedes automatic transmission assembly, but the exact gearbox code/part number and the seller’s “tested/working, low mileage, never opened” claims are not provable from the images. Without the identification plate and proof of testing, a reliable worst-case price cannot be set.
